Subject: Customer request — case study + logo use in exchange for rate-card adjustment

Priyom / Kim,

Quick context: CareVantage is saying they'll sign on a pilot (RDW-2027-0423) if we agree to a 20% off first-year consumption rate-card adjustment. In return they want a 12-month case study, permission to use our logo in their customer-facing materials, and three co-branded social posts.

I've attached the draft case study the customer shared (CareVantage_CaseStudy_Draft_v1.docx) and a short summary of the proposed credit schedule (RDW_Deal_Summary_CreditSchedule.pdf).

Why I’m looping you both:
- Kimberly — legal redlines and any publicity constraints we need to lock down. Does the requested logo + quotes exposure create any IP or exclusivity issues?
- Vivek — this is outside of normal sales thresholds for publicity-for-credit trades; we need an exec ok to proceed.

If we sign, marketing will want final editorial approval (no surprise quotes). Can we get a quick read and an approval path? Customer is asking for a yes/no by COB today.

Thanks,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Customer request — case study + logo use in exchange for rate-card adjustment

Thanks Marissa — quick summary for the thread:
- Deal: CareVantage pilot, estimated $480k TCV first-year.
- Ask: 20% off first-year consumption (applied as a one-time credit) in exchange for a 12-month case study + three co-branded social posts + permission to use our logo and a short quote.
- Risk: discount > standard deal desk threshold; asks for public quote.

Kimberly, can you confirm if the publicity language in the attached draft is acceptable or needs material edits? If legal can provisionally accept our standard MarketingReleaseTemplate with a few redlines, I’ll escalate to Vivek for executive sign-off.

If we don’t get sign-off today, customer indicated they’ll push procurement into next quarter, which risks pricing comps.

– Priyom

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-08-25T12:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Customer request — case study + logo use in exchange for rate-card adjustment

Priyom / Marissa,

I reviewed the draft. High-level legal items before we commit:
1) No exclusivity: the release as written implies a 6-month exclusivity for our segment — must be removed.
2) Quote approvals: we need explicit editorial approval and a right to redact any technical claims that could be inaccurate.
3) Data mentions: the draft includes a line referencing "processing PHI at scale" — we cannot allow claims implying PHI access without separate compliance language and a privacy review.
4) Logo usage: acceptable under a limited, non-endorsement license; need a visual usage guide and size constraints.

I can produce a redlined MarketingReleaseTemplate that: a) strips exclusivity, b) adds explicit approval steps and a 30-day review window, c) replaces sensitive phrasing about PHI with "sensitive customer data" and references our standard compliance blurb.

Legal note: we recommend the discount be structured as a one-time invoice credit (to avoid ongoing pricing precedent) and capped to the first 12 months. Anything longer needs CCO approval.

I’ll attach the redline in ~90 minutes. If you need an interim approval path to tell the customer "we can make this work with exec sign-off and minor legal redlines," you have that.

— Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-08-25T15:01:00-07:00
Subject: Exec sign-off request: CareVantage publicity-for-credit (RDW-2027-0423)

Vivek — sorry to pull you in late. Short ask: approve a one-time 20% first-year credit in exchange for a 12-month case study + logo use + three co-branded social posts. Legal has requested these constraints: no exclusivity, editorial approval, replace PHI phrasing, and limit the credit to the first 12 months (structured as invoice credit).

Why I’m recommending approval:
- TCV ~ $480k first year; material short-term ARR impact but high expansion potential across their enterprise.
- Customer is a reference in a strategic vertical (digital health) — having them on a published case study will materially help our non-sales GTM in healthcare.
- Marketing commits to final editorial control and a standard release template.

Proposed guardrails if you approve:
1) Discount = one-time invoice credit, capped at first 12 months.
2) Marketing must approve final copy; Redwood reserves right to redact any technical claims.
3) Legal to sign final MarketingReleaseTemplate redline.

Customer asked for a yes by COB. If you approve, I’ll send a scoped commitment email to CareVantage and request their signed release.

Thanks for the quick read,
Priyom

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-08-25T17:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exec sign-off request: CareVantage publicity-for-credit (RDW-2027-0423)

Ok to proceed with the concession under the guardrails you laid out. Conditions:
- Credit is one-time, applied to invoices covering the first 12 months only. No multi-year pricing precedent.
- Legal to finalize redlines (no exclusivity, editorial approval, compliance language).
- Marketing must approve final copy before anything is published; Redwood retains right to decline any quote that implies capability claims we do not support.
- If customer requests any additional concessions (extended credit window, exclusivity, or use of competitor names), escalate back to me.

Priyom — go ahead and confirm to CareVantage. Please copy me on the outgoing commitment and include the MarketingReleaseTemplate and the DocuSign link.

Best,
Vivek
